title: Bridge: Quiet Hours Ops Summary (shadow log + handoff)
content:
Summary:

This note captures the quiet-hours operations summary (bridge shadow log) from the night bridge between 2027-03-20 22:00 UTC and 2027-03-21 06:00 UTC, plus the handoff for the morning on-call. Intent is to surface incidents, SLO impacts, mitigation steps taken overnight, and explicit follow-ups for the next rotation. Mostly observational; a couple of follow-ups require product/infra owners.

High-level:
- 2 medium-severity incidents during the window: one transient model-serving latency spike, one embedding pipeline partial retry loop. Both contained within error-budget tolerances but visible to some customers.
- SLO health: 99.85% p99 token latency for hosted-api route "/v1/generate" across the 24h window — just inside SLO but trending up in the last 6h. Error budget consumption for the hosted tier increased by 0.8% overnight.
- No pagers after 03:40 UTC; on-call decided against escalation for the second event after mitigations reduced user-visible errors.

Incidents (abridged):
1) Incident: model-serving latency spike (INC-SRE-2027-03-21-01)
   - Timeline: ~2027-03-21 00:55 UTC start, incident mitigated by 01:20 UTC, final back-to-normal 01:30 UTC.
   - Symptom: sudden increase in p95/p99 generation latency on m04-small-quantized-rt variant in us-west1. Error responses (504 gateway) increased from baseline 0.02% to 0.9% for 30 minutes.
   - Root-cause hypothesis (prelim): background kernel upgrade job on a subset of dedicated hosts caused transient CPU contention + increased GC stalls in the runtime (observed process stalls in perf traces).
   - Mitigations applied: stepped traffic away from affected host pool via routing policy to alternate region (us-east1) and scaled up a warm pool for m04-small-quantized-rt by +20% to absorb burst. Reverted kernel job where possible.
   - Customer impact: small fraction of requests timed out or hit higher latency; customers on dedicated capacity with strict latency SLAs may have seen tail increases. No long-running degradations.
   - Next steps: SRE to gather kernel job logs and host telemetry (Marco). Runtime team to correlate GC stall traces with the deployment (Samir). Draft postmortem if RCA confirms kernel interaction.

2) Incident: embedding pipeline retry-loop (INC-SRE-2027-03-21-03)
   - Timeline: first anomalies at ~03:05 UTC, observed retry amplification until 03:35 UTC, cool-down and steady state by 03:50 UTC.
   - Symptom: upstream datastore (kvs-embedding-store) intermittently returning 503 for range of keys; embedding ingestion retried aggressively, creating backlog and queue pressure in the ingestion worker group.
   - Mitigations applied: placed embedding ingestion workers into limited concurrency mode, enabled delayed exponential backoff in the ingestion orchestrator (hotfix), and scaled read replicas for kvs-embedding-store by +2 nodes.
   - Root-cause hypothesis (prelim): a transient networking flake between the embedding service and the primary replica combined with a bug in the retry supervisor that didn't apply jitter.
   - Customer impact: slight delay in embedding availability for newly submitted items (median delay increased from 12s to 68s for affected keys). No data loss.
   - Next steps: infra/networking to review replica health and tracing (Ellen). Engineering to push fix to retry supervisor to add jitter and max cap (PR reference linked).

SLOs and Metrics Snapshot:
- Hosted API generation endpoints: 24h availability 99.97%. P99 token latency 99.85% (SLO: 99.9% target). Error budget consumed last 7d: 3.6% (still within grace, watch if trend continues).
- Dedicated tier: availability 99.99% (no SLA hits). Tail latency variance concentrated in us-west1 host pool during hour window.
- Embeddings pipeline: ingestion success rate 99.4% over 24h (target 99.5%). Backlog cleared within 45 minutes post-mitigation.

On-call Handoff Notes (for morning responder: Priya):
- Key ongoing items: gather kernel upgrade timeline and host crashloop artifacts (INC-SRE-2027-03-21-01). See host list: hostpool-usw-kernel-03..06 (Marco owns initial collection).
- Watchlist metrics: p99 generation latency (route /v1/generate) - alert threshold at 99.9% over 15m; embedding ingest queue length - alert if > 300 pending.
- Current flags: temporary routing rule applied to steer m04-small-quantized-rt to us-east1; keep this rule for up to 6h to ensure warm pools stable. If warm pool capacity drops below 85% revert and re-evaluate.
- Customer comms: CS ticket CS-7248 flagged by customer on dedicated tier; they saw latency spike. Drafted note in Slack (#cs-ops) summarizing mitigations. Recommend a short follow-up email once RCA is ready.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Collect kernel upgrade job logs and host CPU/IO traces (Marco) — ETA 2027-03-22 EOD.
- Correlate runtime GC traces with request latency spikes and produce timeline (Samir) — ETA 2027-03-23 morning.
- Harden retry supervisor (add jitter + max retry cap) and run canary (Ellen + infra) — PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5231 — ETA 2027-03-24.
- Create postmortem draft if RCA confirms host/kernel interaction (Aisha) — hold until evidence, target draft 2027-03-25.
- Customer follow-up note (CS + SRE) — Priya to coordinate, ETA 2027-03-24.

Operational notes / quick wins:
- Suggestion: add temporary synthetic traffic for m04-small-quantized-rt in us-west1 during rolling kernel upgrades to detect tail spikes early (low cost).
- Recommend adding jitter by default to small-worker retry supervisors; this has shown to reduce amplification in other pipelines.
- Observability gap: need a single-pane timeline linking kernel jobs, host-level telemetry, and request traces. Filing a signal request to observability (Jira SRE-4505).

Open questions:
- Did the kernel upgrade job originate from our automated maintenance window or from a manual intervention? (Marco to confirm).
- Are there any long-running processes on dedicated hosts that might exacerbate GC behavior on the runtime during low-memory events? (Samir to check process lists).

Appendix (links & quick refs):
- Bridge Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0INFR0/MSG3942
- Incident tickets: JIRA-SRE-4498, JIRA-SRE-4501
- Warm pool scaling dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/hosting/warm-pools
- Embedding ingestion queue dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/pipeline/embeddings-queue

Notes to self: this felt like a classic interaction between infra-level changes and runtime sensitivity. Low-friction early detection (synthetic probes + host-change annotations in traces) would have made mitigations faster. For now we have reasonable containment steps and clear owners for follow-up.

If anything is missing from the morning handoff, ping in #sre-handoff and mark with :handoff_check: so we can triage before the daily standup.
